name: Jinamoc seaplane ramp
blurb: A 220 foot beaching ramp of pre-cast concrete and steel.
history:
At the Jinamoc seaplane base, about five miles east of Tacloban, the Navy's first ramp was a submerged pontoon barge; the permanent ramp that replaced it was 220 feet long, of steel and pre-cast concrete. That length is the one cited figure. The 40 foot width, the 1 in 15 slope, the split between concrete slabs and steel decking, the fill, piles, curbs and rails are estimates.

The origin is the underside of the toe, not the waterline; where the water meets the ramp is for the placer to set.

sources.title: Building the Navy's Bases in World War II, ch. XXIX: Advance Bases in the Philippines
